A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodeV and Tool-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO). Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CodeV benchmark evaluations, tool-faithfulness measurements, training and reward ablations, training curves and qualitative trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a tool-output perturbation experiment on V* in Appendix 11 and Table 6.

M1.justification: The CodeV architecture, Python-based actions, SFT-plus-RL pipeline, TAPO objective and reward components remain unchanged. The added perturbations are evaluation interventions, not changes to training or the proposed inference procedure.

E1.justification: Training sources and benchmark datasets are retained. Appendix 11 adds four V* test scenarios with masked, noisy, unrelated or missing tool-output images, extending coverage to altered visual feedback without adding a new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark, faithfulness and ablation experiments. The new perturbation study reuses Pixel-Reasoner and DeepEyes, both already evaluated against CodeV in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds a test-time intervention protocol that perturbs returned tool images and measures percentages of trajectories with changed reasoning tokens, subsequent tool actions or final answers. Existing training settings, benchmark evaluations and crop-faithfulness judging procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix 11 and Table 6 add a substantive diagnostic study testing whether tool outputs influence model behavior, beyond v1's checks that crops contain relevant objects. Four perturbations examine reasoning, action and answer sensitivity across three models. Existing ablations, tool-frequency analyses and qualitative examples remain.

E5.justification: There is no change in seed, repeated-evaluation or uncertainty reporting. The new perturbation results are point percentages without confidence intervals, significance tests or reported repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, faithfulness and ablation values are unchanged. New Table 6 reports additional perturbation outcomes: under masking, reasoning changes in 85.9% of CodeV, 39.7% of Pixel-Reasoner and 5.8% of DeepEyes trajectories; answer changes are 9.6%, 2.1% and 5.2%, respectively. These are new diagnostic results, not improved scores under the original settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations 1–6 and faithfulness aggregation algorithm are unchanged. The new behavioral-change measurements introduce no mathematical derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about TAPO, faithfulness evaluation, benchmark performance and released resources. The perturbation experiment supplies additional support without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix 11 explicitly acknowledges that correct cropping does not establish use of the crop. It interprets CodeV's greater perturbation sensitivity as evidence of reliance on tool outputs and explains relatively stable answers through alternative, sometimes text-only reasoning paths. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix 11 supplies basic construction details for the new experiment: perturb all returned tool images at inference, use Gaussian noise, and use non-overlapping replacement crops. Noise parameters and exact behavioral-change detection procedures are not specified. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware costs, sandbox details, prompts and resource-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including XRPO, Search-o1, CORRECT, hallucination detection and medical-imaging work. The central positioning relative to visual tool agents and process supervision remains unchanged. Updated bibliographic entries for already discussed methods do not represent new evaluated baselines.

P1.justification: v2 inserts the perturbation appendix, renumbers subsequent sections and cross-references, retitles Section 10.1, and makes scattered wording and bibliographic edits. The main narrative is preserved; some new typographical errors appear, including in the Section 2.1 heading.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 6, adds numerical labels to Figure 4's existing bars, and lightly revises Figure 1's illustration and labels. Subsequent tables are renumbered and appendix material reflows, while the other plots and qualitative images are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix 11 and Table 6 strengthen the paper by probing a gap in v1's crop-presence proxy: whether returned evidence affects subsequent behavior. The explicit qualification about correct crops also improves interpretation. The gain remains limited because the study covers only V*, leaves perturbation and behavioral-comparison details incomplete, and reports no uncertainty; sensitivity alone does not establish fully faithful reasoning. These limitations and small editorial regressions do not outweigh the added diagnostic evidence.
